claims.text: Rapid cooling methods such as melt spinning yield predominantly amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 containing incipient crystalline nuclei.
Applying approximately 20 kHz ultrasonic agitation during reheating at 900–1200 K will disrupt embryonic crystalline-cluster formation.
Ultrasonic agitation during reheating will disrupt the growth and coalescence of embryonic crystalline clusters.
Ultrasonic agitation supplies localized mechanical energy that disturbs atomic ordering during reheating.
Disturbing atomic ordering prevents stable crystalline nuclei from forming during reheating.
Kinetic frustration caused by ultrasound limits the alloy's multistep crystallization process.
Limiting multistep crystallization helps maintain the amorphous state.
Ultrasonic treatment will delay the onset of crystallization relative to conventional reheating.
The delayed crystallization onset will appear as an upward shift of crystallization exotherms in DSC.
Ultrasonically treated samples will retain a higher amorphous volume fraction than conventionally reheated samples.
Higher amorphous retention and delayed crystallization indicate improved thermal stability.
Conventional reheating without ultrasound typically produces extensive primary crystallization, earlier DSC exothermic peaks, and lower amorphous retention.
The intervention is expected to be effective only between 900 K and 1200 K during reheating.
The intervention requires an initial cooling rate greater than approximately 10^5 K/s.
An initial cooling rate above approximately 10^5 K/s creates an amorphous-lean substrate.
Uniform ultrasonic-energy penetration may be difficult to achieve in high-temperature metallic samples.
Sample size and configuration may affect the outcome of ultrasonic treatment.
The hypothesis is falsified if ultrasound produces neither a statistically significant upward shift in crystallization onset nor a higher retained amorphous fraction than the untreated control.

contradictions.description: The initial rapidly cooled material is described as predominantly amorphous and the experiment aims to establish an initial amorphous state, whereas the boundary calls the rapidly cooled material an 'amorphous-lean substrate.'
